question.problem: Find the center and radius of the circle whose equation is ${x}^{2}-4x+{y}^{2}-2y=-4.$
question.worked_solution:
To find the center and radius of the circle, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-4x+{y}^{2}-2y & =-4 \\ ({x}^{2}-4x)+({y}^{2}-2y) & =-4 \\ ({x}^{2}-2\cdot 2x+{2}^{2})+({y}^{2}-2\cdot y+{1}^{2}) & =-4+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2} \\ ({x}^{2}-2\cdot 2x+{2}^{2})+({y}^{2}-2\cdot y+{1}^{2}) & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can factor the perfect squares and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2}+(y-1)^{2} & ={1}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(2,1)$ and its radius is $1.$
